explanation: Perform a depth-first traversal and append each value in inorder order. Null children contribute no values.
timeComplexity: O(n) time. Each node is expanded and emitted a constant number of times, with pending work bounded by height.
spaceComplexity: O(h) recursion space plus O(n) output space. The recursion or explicit stack retains pending traversal work; the result stores n values.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract; EPI problem attribution remains in the collection.
correctness: For an empty subtree the result is empty, matching inorder. For a nonempty subtree, recursive induction gives the left subtree’s inorder followed by its root value and the right subtree’s inorder. Those are precisely the three pieces in the definition of inorder traversal. Each node is appended once between its two child traversals.
walkthrough: For tree [16, 7, 25, 2, 11, null, 30], the left subtree contributes 2, 7, 11. Append root 16, then the right subtree contributes 25, 30. Return [2, 7, 11, 16, 25, 30]. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: Null input returns an empty list.
A node with only one child still appears between its left and right portions.
Repeated Data values are visited separately; this is a traversal, not a set.
